title: openai: chat.completions parity — streaming stability, function-calling, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Alex Kim
description: Goal: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with common OpenAI behaviors: stable streaming chunking, explicit role handling, stop token semantics, streaming/aggregated logprobs, function-calling semantics, and response formatting for structured output. Motivation: Customers expect the OpenAI-compatible endpoint to behave like OpenAI's API for migration simplicity and third-party SDK compatibility. Several customers reported mismatches around streaming chunk framing (causing client parser errors) and function_call handling when streaming. This PR consolidates the compatibility surface and hardens streaming behavior. Changes (high level): - Stabilize streaming framing and chunk boundaries: introduce deterministic event boundaries and align the streaming 'delta' events with OpenAI's practice (role/name hints emitted once, content in incremental chunks). - Function calling: add support for the function_call hint and full-function JSON payload streaming. When a model emits a 'function_call' we now stream its name and arguments as structured events and emit a final 'function_call' completion object. - Roles handling: ensure 'system', 'assistant', and 'user' roles are preserved and can be passed via the OpenAI compatibility fields. Fixes edge cases where role was dropped on partial responses. - Stop & logprobs: support stop token semantics server-side and include logprobs in both streaming and aggregated responses when requested. Logprobs are emitted as base64-encoded JSON payloads in the streaming envelope to avoid breaking incremental parsers. - Response formatting: add a compatibility layer to return 'choices' array, 'usage' object, and top-level fields consistent with OpenAI formatting. A new configuration flag openai_compat=true enables the format. - Tests & docs: add unit, integration, and e2e tests exercising parity cases; update docs with migration notes and example payloads. Checklist: - [x] Streaming framing and event shape added - [x] Function calling streaming coverage - [x] stop/logprobs behavior implemented and tested - [x] Response formatting and top-level OpenAI fields - [x] Backwards compatibility smoke tests - [x] Docs and SDK example updates Compatibility notes: This is opt-in behind the openai_compat flag and the /v1/chat.completions compatibility handler. Existing Redwood native endpoints are unchanged. Function-calling behavior follows OpenAI semantics; callers using Redwood-native function integrations should test the new path before migrating. Risk/rollback: Low. Feature gated and covered by e2e tests. If issues arise the compatibility handler can be disabled without impact to native APIs.
